main_text.p: Dum fortuna fuit. feror huc, & litore curuo Moenia prima loco, fatis ingressus iniquis, Æneadáfque meo nomen de nomine fingo.
main_text.head: MACEDONES THRACIBVS funt vicini ad Auftrum.
Macedonia, quæ & Æmathia dicta est, generalis descriptio.
main_text.p: Tristior Æmonijs miles digressus ab oris, Aemonia. Claud. in Rufinum lib. 2. Tangebat Macedûm fines, murósque subibat Thessalonica tuos. Dionysius. —Macedoniaq; urbes

Post has autem apparent vertices niuosi Æmi Æmus, Thracij, huius è regione ad flatum Zephyri, Dodona regio immensa extenta est. Qua iuga deuexus Pharsalica porrigit Æmus. Lucan. lib. 6. Romanas acies iterum videre Philippi: Philippi op. Virg. Georg. lib. 3. Nec fuit indignum superis, bis sanguine nostro Æmathiam, & latos Æmi pinguescere campos. Æmathia.
main_text.head: Amyrus fluuius Magnesiæ regionis prope Macedoniam.
main_text.p: —attollit tondentes pabula Magnes Valer. lib. 2, Argonaut. Campus equos: vidisse putant Dolopeia busta, Intrantémque Amyron curuas quæsita per oras Æquora flumineo cuius redeuntia vento Vela legant.

page.notes: Marginal notes are partly cut off and faint; the reading of the note beside "Aemonia" and "Claud. in Rufinum" is approximate. The Greek ornament above the second heading is a decorative border and is not transcribed. Some verse line-ends are uncertain.
